items.title: Root-L2 Hellinger distance for dominated laws
items.statement: For probability laws P and Q with supplied densities p and q against one sigma-finite measure, define h(P,Q)^2 = integral (sqrt(p)-sqrt(q))^2. The companion comparison theorem proves the expression is independent of the common dominating measure.
items.strategy: Definition: state the common sigma-finite dominating measure and the supplied finite-valued density representatives; make the root-L2 convention explicit.

items.title: Hellinger invariance and comparison with library total variation
items.statement: The root-L2 Hellinger expression is invariant under replacing one common sigma-finite dominating measure by another, and under the library convention TV(P,Q)=sup_A |P(A)-Q(A)| it satisfies TV(P,Q) <= h(P,Q) and h(P,Q)^2 <= 2 TV(P,Q).
items.strategy: Direct: compare both common-measure expressions to the finite canonical measure P+Q, derive TV as half the L1 density distance, then apply Cauchy-Schwarz and a pointwise square-root inequality.

items.title: Posterior consistency from KL support and uniformly summable tests
items.statement: For a well-specified dominated IID Bayesian model with a proper prior, jointly measurable normalized likelihood density, positive mass in every KL neighborhood, and for each metric-separated complement tests whose type-I and uniform type-II errors are summable, the posterior mass of that complement tends to zero almost surely. Under AC, KL support also implies Hellinger support through h^4 <= 2 KL under the library conventions.
items.strategy: Direct: prove an almost-sure exponential lower bound for the posterior denominator by Jensen and the IID strong law; amplify the given tests by independent blocks using the bounded-variable Hoeffding MGF bound; split the posterior numerator, integrate its tested part by Tonelli, and apply Markov plus Borel-Cantelli. Use Pinsker only for the separate KL-to-Hellinger support consequence.

items.title: Identifiability and KL support do not replace testability
items.statement: An identifiable, well-specified dominated IID Bernoulli model can have KL support at its truth yet fail posterior consistency for a metric on its law space when no uniformly consistent tests exist.
items.strategy: Counterexample: use a countable injective Bernoulli family converging to the truth in Hellinger distance, a discrete metric on the distinct laws, and a proper prior that omits the truth but charges every KL neighborhood; prove product-law alternatives become indistinguishable while the posterior remains on the metric-separated prior support.

title: Hellinger geometry and posterior consistency — Examples

items.title: A finite identifiable model with posterior consistency
items.statement: In a two-point Bernoulli model with distinct success probabilities, positive prior mass at the true law and exponentially consistent tests verify the posterior consistency theorem's hypotheses.
items.strategy: Verification: check injectivity, KL support, and the two Bernoulli tail bounds, then apply the locally proved posterior consistency theorem.

items.title: The factor of two between density L1 and library total variation
items.statement: For two disjoint point-mass laws, density L1 distance is 2, event-supremum total variation is 1, and root-L2 Hellinger distance is sqrt(2), so h^2 <= 2 TV is sharp.
items.strategy: Verification: compute both densities on a two-point space, take the event supremum, and evaluate the two Hellinger summands exactly.
